title: ReversibleMutationEnvelope
description: The envelope a mutation must carry to be admitted. `inverse_spec` is the field ADR 0024 implies and nothing previously required: either a deterministic inverse with a state probe, or an irreversible exemption carrying an attestation verified over `subject`. Read by bin/idp-reversibility-gate; the ledger door (propose_mutation -> verify_mutation -> seal_mutation -> admit_mutation) is what consumes it.

mutation_id.description: Ledger id. Deliberately not a fixed hex shape: the executor's ledger ids are opaque strings (docs/specs/2026-09-15-typed-multidomain-mutation-ledger-door.md), and pinning a format here would refuse correct work (LAW 38).

subject.description: The digest an irreversible exemption's attestation must be signed over. Required in practice when inverse_spec.type is irreversible_exemption; the gate refuses an exemption whose subject is absent.

target.description: What the mutation acts on, e.g. deployment/payment-processor.

verification_probe.description: A deterministic state assertion the rollback path can run, e.g. `kubectl get deployment payment-processor -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}' == 2`. Not a description of intent.

justification.description: Why this mutation cannot be reversed. The human's answer to 'why is there no undo'.

attestation.description: A Sigstore bundle or the estate ed25519 envelope, verified by sovereign.verifier.verify_attestation over `subject`. NOT a token with a magic prefix -- a prefix check is not authentication.
